Sitting just inside the play-off positions, Shakhtar Donetsk look to enhance their standing in the UEFA Champions League (UCL) as they take on a Fenerbahçe side high on a historic win in the last round.

Match News and Current Form

Concerns might be brewing over Shakhtar Donetsk’s form, after a 1-1 draw with Livyi Bereh on Friday left them without a win in three games (D2, L1) for the first time since October 2025. That run started with a narrow 1-0 loss to Sporting in this competition and means the Ukrainian side sit on four points at the half-way stage of the league phase (W1, D1, L2). The victory was a 3-1 success over AEK at their UCL home of Stamford Bridge, with the Miners unable to play matches on home soil due to the conflict in their homeland, and those three strikes account for 75% of the goals scored by Arda Turan’s side in the league phase, with only two teams starting this round having netted fewer times.

Fenerbahçe ended their 18-year wait for a victory in the main draw of the UCL when they beat Liverpool 3-2 in their last league phase outing. That victory sparked something of a turnaround in their competitive form (W2, D1), but as they still remain some way off the title pace in the Turkish top flight, they still have much room for improvement. It’s difficult to see their run continuing here as, despite losing only one of their last 11 European matches (W6, D4), Fenerbahçe have failed to win any of their last 12 UCL proper away games (D3, L9).

Head-to-Head History

Shakhtar are unbeaten across two prior H2Hs (W1, D1), while they’re also unbeaten in their 11 matches against Turkish clubs (W10, D1), winning each of their last seven.

Key Players to Watch and Missing Players

Shakhtar’s Marlon Gomes has made a UCL-high 18 tackles this season but has also committed nine fouls along the way - only three players made more in the first four rounds. Mason Greenwood has netted four goals across his last three Fenerbahçe appearances and is unbeaten across the last ten matches in which he has been on target (W7, D3).

Shakhtar have no fresh injury concerns, while it seems likely that Nathan Aké will be missing for Fenerbahçe.

The struggling pair of Slavia Prague and Villarreal will see this meeting as a golden opportunity to improve their chances of qualifying for the UEFA Champions League (UCL) knockouts.

Match News and Current Form

Slavia’s 19-year wait for a UCL main draw victory continues after their 2-1 defeat to Arsenal left them languishing near the bottom of the standings (D1, L3). The Red and Whites have recorded a Czech record of 19 consecutive European games without winning (D6, L13), and with trips to Bayern Munich and Porto ahead of them, they badly need to take their superb domestic form into European football. Slavia scored an impressive 15 goals in their last four domestic games (W4), and although they’ve recently been competitive at home in the UCL, losing both home fixtures this term by one-goal margins, they’re now on a club record run of ten consecutive home European matches without victory (D4, L6).

Villarreal’s 6-0 defeat to PSG on matchday four left them outside the top-24 with just three points (W1, L3), whilst their defensive frailties were again on display at the weekend when they squandered an early 2-0 lead to lose 3-2 to Barcelona. That has been a common theme throughout their recent European journeys, given Villarreal have already scored eight UCL goals this term - three more than they managed in the entirety of the league phase last season - but have now lost 12 of their last 14 games in this competition proper (W1, D1). That includes defeat in each of their last seven on the road, a record for any Spanish club.

Head-to-Head History

Villarreal are unbeaten across the two previous H2Hs (W1, D1), winning 2-0 here in 2017/18.

Slavia have injury concerns over Štěpán Chaloupek, Lukáš Provod and Danijel Šturm, while David Moses suffered an injury during Saturday’s 2-0 win over Sigma Olomouc. Juan Foyth and Gerard Moreno are among Villarreal’s likely absentees.

With their UEFA Champions League (UCL) campaign heading in the wrong direction, Azerbaijan champions Sabah face the unenviable task of needing to take points from five-time UCL kings Barcelona.

Match News and Current Form

Sabah come into this match feeling a little more confident after ending a five-game winless run in all competitions (D2, L3) with a 5-1 domestic league win over Sumqayit on Friday. Valdas Dambrauskas’ men now need to carry that form forward into matchday five after a 4-1 defeat to Viking earlier this month had them placed outside the top-24 at the halfway point of the league phase. Their sole victory (2-0 against Slavia Prague) came at their UEFA home venue, Baku Olympic Stadium, where they’ll be hoping to upset the odds despite the dreadful record that Azerbaijani clubs possess in major European competition against teams from the ‘big five’ leagues (W2, D10, L39).

Barcelona pulled off an outrageous comeback to beat Villarreal 3-2 on Sunday, extending their winning run to four matches in the process. That streak includes a 3-0 success against Aston Villa in the UCL, where the Spanish side are on course to secure automatic qualification for the Round of 16 after three wins in four attempts (L1). Hansi Flick’s men will now attempt to register back-to-back UCL clean sheets for the first time since 2023 and, whilst they haven’t recorded a UCL clean sheet on the road in ten matches, an impressive record of seven wins from eight competitive away fixtures this term (L1) gives reason to suggest they will at least come out on top.

This is the first time Sabah have faced Spanish opposition as well as Barcelona’s first tussle with a club from Azerbaijan.

FLASHSCORE PREVIEW

Atlético Madrid have been struggling at this stage of the UEFA Champions League (UCL) for a while now, but salvation may await when a Viking side who struggle on the road in Europe visit the Spanish capital. 

Match News and Current Form

Atlético bounced back from successive defeats before the international break with a 3-0 win over Getafe on Sunday night to hang on to the coattails of the early La Liga pacesetters. They’re nowhere near the top of the UCL league phase table though, after a slow start to their campaign has seen them pick up four points from the opening four rounds, contributing to a record of just one win in their last six UCL league phase outings (D2, L3). They have at least won ten of the last 13 matches they hosted at this stage (L3), but it's worth noting that one of those defeats came against Norwegian opposition in the form of Bodø/Glimt last season!

Viking lost crucial ground on Bodø/Glimt in the Eliteserien over the weekend, as their 3-2 defeat to Tromsø left them three points adrift at the summit with just three games remaining. They’ll have to quickly park that disappointment if they’re to build on their first-ever win in the UCL proper against Sabah in the last round, but that appears a tall order on the road, where Viking have won just two of their last 13 European games (D4, L7). Two of those defeats came in this season’s league phase, though both did see Viking get on the scoresheet, as they’ve done in a club-record 12 successive European matches.

Head-to-Head History

Prior to last season’s loss against Bodø/Glimt, Atlético had won all six matches against Norwegian opposition. Viking lost their two previous visits to Spain without scoring.

After his goal against Getafe, Atlético’s Álex Baena has now opened the scoring with each of his last three goals for club or country, though only one of his last seven strikes came in a home game. Anything positive about Viking may come through Zlatko Tripić, who has been involved in five of Viking's nine UCL goals (G2, A3), while his last 23 club strikes came in games which produced over 2.5 goals.

Cristian Romero missed Atlético’s game on Sunday, while Viking appear to be at full strength.

FLASHSCORE PREVIEW

A bruised and battered Bayern Munich side look to close in on the UEFA Champions League (UCL) top eight when they travel to a Lille side desperately struggling at Europe’s top table.

Match News and Current Form

A 1-0 Ligue 1 loss to Lyon on Saturday means Lille return to the UCL on the back foot, a familiar feeling in this competition for a side who sat second-bottom after the first four matchdays (D1, L3). A goalless draw with Bodø/Glimt last time out ended a club-record run of five successive European defeats for the Mastiffs, but only once have they ever endured a longer winless streak on the continent than their current six-match slump (D1, L5). Those negative omens follow Lille home as they’ve also lost a club record four successive major European home matches, while they could be beaten in their opening three home fixtures of a UCL campaign for just the second time here.

The previous instance came back in 2012/13 and included a defeat to Bayern, who travel to France after a disappointing 1-1 draw with Cologne on Friday which saw arguably their two best players go down injured. Manager Vincent Kompany was back on the touchline at least, and the Belgian has overseen an unbeaten start to the Bavarians’ UCL campaign (W2, D2), with their only two defeats in this competition since the start of last season coming against 2025/26 finalists PSG and Arsenal (W13, D3). The reversal to PSG was Bayern’s last defeat on the road in any competition (W7, D3), while they’ve scored 2+ goals in 12 of their last 13 UCL games at any venue.

Head-to-Head History

Bayern won both prior H2Hs, which came in the UCL back in 2012. Lille have won just two of their last 11 matches against German opponents in any competition (D3, L6) and have never beaten one at home in the UCL (D1, L2).

Key Players to Watch and Missing Players

Lille veteran Olivier Giroud has played a career-high nine UCL matches against Bayern, netting three times along the way, while two of his three strikes this term opened the scoring. Luis Díaz looks set to return here and shoulders great responsibility for Bayern as he makes a 50th appearance in this competition - the last 11 UCL games he scored in produced over 2.5 goals.

Lille’s ex-Bayern defender Tanguy Nianzou was forced off injured at the weekend, a fate that also befell Bayern duo Michael Olise and Harry Kane, with the Englishman set for an extended spell on the sidelines.

PSG have a stunning winning run behind them as they prepare to host a Roma side who have long since struggled on the road in the UEFA Champions League (UCL). 

Match News and Current Form

PSG have made light work of the UCL so far as they go in search of a third successive European crown, winning each of their four league phase outings so far. The alarming ease at which they’ve won those games is evidenced by their 20-goal haul, the most any club has ever managed in the first four matches of a UCL group/league phase, and with the record for an entire such campaign standing at 28, it’s hard to see the Parisians not eclipsing that. A phenomenal 12-match winning competitive run should serve as another confidence booster for them, and with a club-record 14-match unbeaten UCL run behind them (W10, D4), belief is bound to be sky high that they can eclipse Lyon’s French record 14-match undefeated streak in such games here.

Roma might not possess the same length of winning run as PSG, but four successive Serie A victories have kept them firmly in the title hunt. They too have had no issues on the scoring front, rattling in 3+ goals in all four of those wins, with a 3-2 UCL defeat against Manchester United on matchday four sandwiched in between, a result which means Roma have won only one of their last 11 away games in the UCL proper (D2, L8). Conceding in 33 successive UCL road trips certainly hasn’t helped their cause, but salvation could come in a trip to France, as Roma have won on both of their UCL main draw visits to this country.

Head-to-Head History

These sides have never met before. PSG are unbeaten in five home matches against Italian clubs (W3, D2), winning each of the last three, although Roma have never been beaten by French opposition in the UCL proper (W3, D1).

FLASHSCORE PREVIEW

Inter Milan have recovered from a dreadful start to their UEFA Champions League (UCL) campaign and now look to overtake opponents Stuttgart, who have stumbled after winning their opening two fixtures. 

Match News and Current Form

Inter were denied at the death by a late penalty in a thrilling 4-4 draw at Atalanta on Sunday, falling three points behind Serie A leaders Lazio. The Nerazzurri are still in good form, having won six of their last eight competitive games (D1, L1), including back-to-back UCL wins without conceding, which have helped Cristian Chivu’s men bounce back from a two-game losing start in this edition. Inter will expect that positive run to continue here amid a decent record across their last 19 league phase matches which have produced no stalemates (W13, L6), a trend which could continue here as they are yet to draw a competitive match this season as hosts (W7, L1).

Stuttgart come into this game after a goalless draw against Schalke last weekend, although Sebastian Hoeneß’ men have been beaten in just one of their last five competitive games (W3, D1). That defeat came on matchday four of this competition courtesy of a 2-0 loss to Galatasaray, meaning they enter this game winless in two UCL games after winning their first two. Looking to arrest that dip as they bid to qualify for the UCL knockout stage, Stuttgart have a tough job on their hands in a country where they often struggle, albeit they might put up a good fight considering they haven't failed to score in back-to-back UCL games since 2007, while their record in the last eight UCL trips (W4, L4) also suggests we can expect a result either way.

Head-to-Head History

This is the first H2H and while Inter are unbeaten in their last three UCL games against German clubs (W2, D1), Stuttgart have just one win in their last nine away matches against Italian opponents (D2, L6).

Hot Stats and Streaks

Eleven of Inter’s 16 competitive matches this season saw the match-opening goal arrive within the first 20 minutes.

Inter have never lost a home match in the UCL proper when they led at half-time (W29, D3).

Stuttgart’s last eight UCL matches averaged four goals per game.

Only three of Stuttgart’s last 11 competitive matches saw both teams score.

Key Players to Watch and Missing Players

Lautaro Martínez returned from injury at the weekend and could be hoping for a starting role, as seven of his last eight UCL goals have come at home, but both of his strikes this season came in the defeat to Club Brugge. Deniz Undav has been a key figure for Stuttgart in the UCL this season (G1, A2, YC1), with his three goal contributions coming in two wins.

Hakan Çalhanoğlu was forced off injured in Inter’s last match, while Piotr Zieliński missed that game completely. Luca Jaquez was absent from Stuttgart’s game at the weekend.

FLASHSCORE PREVIEW

After suffering the joint-heaviest defeat by any Manchester United manager in their first game in charge, Mauricio Pochettino returns to the UEFA Champions League (UCL) stage with a tough trip to Sporting CP.

Match News and Current Form

Five successive wins in all competitions - the last two of which came under new manager Paulo Fonseca - mean Sporting return to the UCL in good form as they look to break into the top eight of the league phase table (W3, L1). None of Fonseca’s five permanent predecessors won their first UCL game, but the Lions must fancy their chances of ending that run here given that they’ve won six of their last eight home matches in this competition (L2). It seems almost certain that they’ll be on the scoresheet in any case as Sporting have scored in 22 successive group/league phase matches - an all-time record for a Portuguese team.

No team in Europe look less equipped to deal with Sporting’s attack than Manchester United, who were thrashed 4-0 by Liverpool on Sunday in a chastening touchline debut for Pochettino. The Red Devils are now winless in a negative club record nine Premier League games and have conceded 34 goals in all competitions this season - more than any other side in a top-five European league. United were at least victorious on matchday four of the UCL and sit in the qualification places pre-round (W2, L2), and though their only clean sheet of the campaign came in this competition, they’ve failed to win their last six UCL away matches (D2, L4) and are yet to win a competitive game on the road all season (D3, L5).

Head-to-Head History

Sporting’s only win in four previous H2Hs (L3) came way back in March 1964 (5-0), with United now unbeaten in 13 successive matches against Portuguese opponents (W9, D4).

Sporting goalkeeper Rui Silva starts the matchday with a UCL-high save percentage (85.7), but he’s lost all three of his prior European meetings with United. Sporting seem to have no fresh issues, while United are without the suspended Matheus Cunha.
